3.

sentences.text:
4. On 06.11.2024, the following order was passed:-
"1. Mr. Rajesh Kumar Mishra, Advocate has filed short counter affidavit and his Vakalatnama on behalf of opposite party No.2, is taken on record.
2. Heard Mr. Ashutosh Pandey, learned counsel for the applicants, Mr. Rajesh Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 and learned AGA for the State.

3. The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed to quash the charge sheet dated 08.03.2017 and cognizance/summoning order dated 04.09.2017 as well as entire criminal proceeding of Crl. Case No.1622 of 2017 (State vs. Samshir and others)
arising out of Case Crime No. 0575 of 2016 under Sections 498A, 323 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, P.S. Etmaddaula, District Agra on the basis of compromise dated 20.06.2024.
4. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that the parties have amicably settled their dispute and a compromise has been entered into between the parties.
In this regard, a compromise affidavit of both the parties has been filed before the court concerned, copy of the same has been annexed as Annexure No.5 of this application.
Therefore, continuance of proceedings against the applicants would futile exercise and wastage of time of the Court and will be abuse of process of law.

Hence,
proceedings of the aforesaid case be quashed in the light of law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Gian Singh v. State of Punjab reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303.
5.

entities.text: Gian Singh v. State of Punjab reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for opposite party no.2 also does not dispute the correctness of the submissions made by the learned counsel for the applicants.
6. Whether a compromise has taken place or not can at best be ascertained by the court, where the proceedings are pending, after ensuring the presence of the parties before it.
7. In view of the above, both the parties are directed to appear before the court below along with copy of compromise deed as well as a certified copy of this order within two weeks from today.

It is expected that the trial court may fix a date for the verification of the compromise and after ensuring the presence of parties, pass an appropriate order with respect to the same in accordance with law, as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a period of one month from today.

While passing the order verifying the compromise, the concerned court shall also record the statement Lalu @ Samshir And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142592989/
2 of the parties as to whether all the terms and conditions mentioned in the original compromise deed, so filed, have been fulfilled or not?

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. Upon due verification of compromise, the court below may pass appropriate order in that regard and send a report to this Court.

9. Put up this case on 05.12.2024, as fresh, at 02:00 p.m., showing the name of Mr.
Rajesh Kumar Mishra in the cause list as counsel for opposite party no.2.
10.
Till then, no coercive measure shall be taken against the applicants in the aforesaid case."

5. In compliance of the aforesaid order dated 06.11.2024, the concerned Court of learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.8, Agra has verified the compromise vide order dated 27.11.2024.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.8, Agra
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Certified copy of the aforesaid compromise verification order dated 27.11.2024 has been annexed on page-11 of the supplementary affidavit filed by the learned counsel for the applicants in the Court today.

6. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that since the compromise entered between the parties has been verified by the court below, the entire proceedings of the aforesaid criminal case may be quashed by this Court.

7. Learned A.G.A. for the State as well as learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 also accept that the parties have entered into a compromise and the copy of the same has also been enclosed along with verification order, they have no objection, if the proceedings in the aforesaid case are quashed.

8. This Court is not unmindful of the following judgements of the Apex Court:
(i). B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and Another; (2003)4 SCC 675,
(ii). Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation; (2008) 9 SCC 677,
(iii). Manoj Sharma Vs. State and Others; (2008) 16 SCC 1,
(iv). Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab; (2012); 10 SCC 303,
(v). Narindra Singh and others Vs. State of Punjab; ( 2014) 6 SCC 466,
9.

arising out of Case Crime No.0575 of 2016, under Sections 498-A, 323 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P.
Act, Police Station- Etmaddaula, District- Agra as well as stay the further proceeding of the aforesaid case, pending before the court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Court No.08, Agra, on the basis of compromise, are hereby quashed.
